decisions.reason: As a newly launched feature that directly complements the firm's secure-identity platform, it is likely to be retained because its strategic fit and the firm's likely slack reduce pressure to cut it quickly despite limited market evidence.

The identity-bound wallet is central to the firm's ecosystem vision, so management would likely keep it while learning from the market, although payments are demanding enough to create some risk if early results miss aspirations.

The NFC login authenticator is the most niche and potentially harder-to-scale offering in the set, so it faces the highest drop risk if uptake disappoints, but its security fit still makes short-run retention more likely than immediate withdrawal.

A secure payment and wallet framework sits close to the firm's core platform capabilities and had standalone website prominence, which suggests results or expectations strong enough to keep it on the market.
This product appears to embody the firm's main strategic direction toward secure multi-service super-app ecosystems, so behavioral-theory logic implies very little incentive to drop it after launch.
The application-shielding library is tightly aligned with the firm's long-built security expertise and had its own page, making it likely to meet internal aspirations well enough to retain.
